_comment: Text/image-to-video via Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B, using ComfyUI's OFFICIAL reference
graph for this specific model (Comfy-Org/workflow_templates:
templates/video_wan2_2_5B_ti2v.json - verified against the live file at
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/templates/video_wan2_2_5B_ti2v.json).
This REPLACES wan-image-to-video.json for TI2V-5B specifically. That file
was built for the Wan 2.1/2.2 14B I2V models' node structure
(WanImageToVideo + a separate CLIPVisionLoader/CLIPVisionEncode chain),
which is architecturally different from TI2V-5B and does not condition on
the starting image correctly for this model - confirmed by a live test
that produced a video with literally zero resemblance to the input image
(the wrong node ran, at the wrong output resolution, effectively ignoring
the reference frame). TI2V-5B's real image-conditioning node is
Wan22ImageToVideoLatent, and it does NOT use clip_vision at all - the
official template has no CLIPVisionLoader/CLIPVisionEncode nodes.
ModelSamplingSD3 (shift=8, the official template's own default) is also
required for TI2V-5B specifically - it was missing entirely from the old
workflow, which likely also contributed to the bad output.
VHS_VideoCombine (not the official template's CreateVideo/SaveVideo pair)
is kept for the final mux step, since ComfyUIVideoProvider's polling/
download code already expects that node's output shape and the
VideoHelperSuite pack is already required/installed for the other Wan
workflow - no reason to introduce a second output mechanism.
STILL UNVERIFIED end-to-end as of this file's creation (built from the
official reference graph + this project's own template-placeholder
convention, not yet run) - the previous file's own bad live-test result is
exactly why a second unverified workflow deserves the same caution, not
less. Test a short (2-3s) clip first and confirm the output actually
resembles the starting image before trusting this for a real episode.
REQUIRES (same as wan-image-to-video.json's model files, minus clip_vision):
1. wan2.2_ti2v_5B model in models/diffusion_models/
2. umt5_xxl text encoder in models/text_encoders/
3. Wan 2.2's own VAE (wan2.2_vae.safetensors, NOT wan_2.1_vae.safetensors)
in models/vae/
4. ComfyUI-VideoHelperSuite custom node pack (for VHS_VideoCombine)
length is the frame count, not seconds - the caller (ComfyUIVideoProvider)
converts the scene's target duration into a frame count using {{FPS}}
before filling this template.
